54ed4ddef4e4bf24833abb72da25e5acbcd9c14a.why: Counter-anchoring retrieval rationale to contrast gastrointestinal obstruction with other potential causes of nausea and vomiting

evidence_chain.link: The presence of adhesions is a known complication of abdominal surgery, which supports the diagnosis of bowel obstruction (B1).
evidence_chain.quote: Intraabdominal adhesions in included studies involved any adhesions related to the access of the surgeons to the planned uterine incision

evidence_chain.link: The absence of significant findings on abdominal ultrasound and contrast-enhanced abdomen argues against a diagnosis of gastrointestinal motility disorder (B2).
evidence_chain.quote: Abdominal ultrasound and a contrast-enhanced abdomen were normal except for slight fecal impaction

ranked_facts.why: The presence of prior abdominal surgery (F18) is a risk factor for adhesions, which can cause bowel obstruction (B1). In contrast, gastrointestinal motility disorders (B2) are less likely to be directly related to prior abdominal surgery.
